_comment: Constants and formulas that were previously hardcoded (differently, in several places) across ad hoc scripts. Consolidated here so the whole pipeline and any future game engine reads the same numbers. Expanded to cover the full ruleset (turn order, movement, faction modes, alliances, victory) after discovering data/rules.json was only a partial distillation of reference/Global Cataclysm Design Doc.odt -- see docs/GAME_ARCHITECTURE.md for how this maps onto the engine.

setup.stacking_cap_scope: a starting-setup purchase limit only (not an in-game limit): every unit purchased at a territory counts against that territory's cap, including naval units and any air unit riding an Aircraft Carrier's escort, even though those deploy to a sea zone rather than the land territory itself. See production.per_turn_deploy_cap_formula for the separate, ongoing (post-setup) rule.
setup.naval_purchase_rule: naval units may only be purchased at a coastal territory (has >=1 adjacent sea zone) and deploy to that sea zone, not the land territory
setup.no_shared_sea_zones_rule: no two factions may deploy naval units (or carrier-based aircraft) to the same sea zone in the starting setup
setup.excluded_naval_zones_note: sea zone id 43 (Caspian Sea) never hosts a naval deployment, default or override, in any starting-setup scenario. The underlying reason (landlocked, no real naval access) is permanent, not setup-only -- every bot's purchase policy also treats this list as off-limits for the rest of the game, not just at setup (see bots.purchase_policy and engine.bots.policy.excluded_naval_purchase_zones); this is a bot-policy choice, not an engine-level restriction, so a human player is not blocked from it.
setup.carrier_escort_rule: every purchased Aircraft Carrier must have at least 1 escorting Fighter or Bomber, which deploys to the carrier's own sea zone instead of a land territory
setup.mandatory_land_unit_rule: every land territory with a foreign-faction land neighbor must have at least 1 land unit (Infantry, Mechanized Infantry, or Armor) at setup -- does not need to be specifically Infantry
setup.unit_diversity_rule: each faction must purchase at least 6 of the 8 purchasable unit types in its starting setup; data/factions.json's per-faction 'focus' list guides which types are emphasized (by spend/quantity), not which types are excluded
setup.leftover_budget_rule: spend the full per-faction budget; when there is a small remainder that can't buy a whole new unit, upgrade an existing Infantry to Mechanized Infantry to use it up

turn_order_note: One faction's full turn is these 7 phases in order; engine/state.py's Phase enum names them 1:1. Only active_factions() (mode HUMAN or BOT) actually cycle through them -- DEFENSIVE and NEUTRAL factions are skipped entirely as the ACTIVE faction (no Purchase, no moves, nothing), though DEFENSIVE still fights back normally as a defender when attacked (see faction_modes). GameState.global_turn increments exactly once per active faction's turn, which is what combat.recovery_rule's `num_factions` means -- len(active_factions()), not a fixed count of all 6 factions. Each faction's turn is announced by a "Start of Turn" step (which round, which turn) before Purchase -- a presentation step of the server's phase queue (server/stepper.py START_OF_TURN), not an engine phase: it changes nothing and has no rules. Rollback (phase_confirmation) only ever applies to Purchase, Combat Move, and Non-Combat Move -- the other four phases are either irreversible (dice already rolled) or fully automatic/derived, with no player choice left to undo. See game_start_settings for the two of these 7 phases that can be skipped entirely on a faction's own first turn.

game_start_settings.randomize_play_order: default True. Chosen once, at game creation (engine.setup.build_game_state's randomize_play_order/rng params) -- shuffles the order factions are inserted into GameState.factions, which is what active_factions() cycles through (dict insertion order) and what combat.contested_territory_rule's capture-claim tie-break uses as 'turn order.' Not itself remembered as a flag on GameState afterward -- only its EFFECT (the shuffled order) persists, the same way it would if the order had simply been typed in that way to begin with.
game_start_settings.allow_combat_moves_first_turn: default False. Stored on GameState (unlike randomize_play_order, checked on every relevant turn, not just at setup) and enforced by GameEngine.advance_phase(): if the ACTIVE faction is currently on its own first turn (FactionState.turns_taken == 0 -- incremented by advance_turn() only when THAT faction's turn concludes, so this is per-faction, not just true for whoever moves first in the play order) and this is False, advance_phase() skips Combat Move entirely -- GameState.phase goes straight from Purchase to Combat Resolution, and never becomes COMBAT_MOVE that turn at all. submit_combat_moves/confirm_combat_moves need no extra guard of their own for this -- they already refuse to run outside the Combat Move phase.
game_start_settings.allow_noncombat_moves_first_turn: default True. Same mechanism as allow_combat_moves_first_turn, for Non-Combat Move -- advance_phase() skips straight from Combat Resolution to Capture Territory when False and it's the active faction's first turn.
game_start_settings.combat_resolution_never_skipped: Combat Resolution itself is NEVER skipped by either setting -- it isn't a 'move,' just auto-resolving whatever's currently contested on the board (declared_battles), regardless of whether the active faction submitted a fresh combat move this turn. A faction on its own combat-move-disabled first turn can still be attacked by someone else beforehand and have units of its own already sitting in a contested territory (e.g. an ally's earlier fight) -- Combat Resolution still runs for that.
game_start_settings.driver_implication: a driver loop must be PHASE-AWARE, not a fixed 7-call sequence -- check GameState.phase before calling into a given phase's action (e.g. only call the Combat Move handler if GameState.phase == Phase.COMBAT_MOVE), since advance_phase() may have already skipped past it. See engine/bots/driver.py's play_to_completion for a worked example.
game_start_settings.max_alliance_size: default 2. A CONFIGURED CEILING, not the value actually enforced -- GameEngine._effective_max_alliance_size() further caps it to (len(active_factions()) - 1), recomputed fresh on every invite_to_alliance call, not just once at setup (confirmed this session). An alliance can never include literally every faction still in the game, since that would make forming it identical to the game ending (victory.game_end_rule); this is what enforces that, rather than a fixed 1-5 range. As factions are eliminated over the course of the game the effective cap shrinks, progressively restricting what NEW alliances can form or grow into -- but this NEVER dissolves an existing alliance that's already larger than the current effective value; only invite_to_alliance's own validation consults it. Not range-validated by engine.setup.build_game_state itself (a caller-trusted value -- passing something like 5 in a 3-faction game is harmless, not an error, since the effective cap starts at 2 either way).
game_start_settings.can_withdraw_from_alliances: default True. Stored on GameState, read by GameEngine.withdraw_from_alliance -- when False, withdrawing raises ValueError (a faction that joins an alliance under this setting can never leave it, short of elimination).
game_start_settings.can_rejoin_alliances: default False. Stored on GameState, read by GameEngine.invite_to_alliance -- when False, FactionState.former_allies (populated by withdraw_from_alliance) blocks a withdrawn faction from ever again sharing an alliance with any of its former co-members; see alliances.rejoin_ban.

orchestration.advance_phase: GameEngine.advance_phase() steps GameState.phase to the next one in this fixed 7-phase sequence -- call it once the active faction's work for the current phase is done, before starting the next phase's calls. A no-op once Alliances is reached. Can skip Combat Move and/or Non-Combat Move entirely for the active faction's own first turn -- see game_start_settings.
orchestration.advance_turn: GameEngine.advance_turn() -- call once, right after process_game_end_check, at the end of the Alliances phase -- closes out the active faction's turn: resets ITS OWN units' has_moved_combat/has_moved_noncombat flags, clears it from every phase-confirmation guard set (_purchases_confirmed and its four siblings), and increments its FactionState.turns_taken (see game_start_settings). None of those resets happen anywhere else in the engine -- without this call, a unit that moved once could never move again for the rest of the game, and a faction could only ever complete each phase once, EVER, not once per turn. Then advances active_faction to the next one in active_factions() (wrapping around, and dynamically skipping anyone eliminated since this faction's turn began), bumps global_turn, and resets phase to Purchase. Raises if the game is already over or this isn't called at the end of Alliances.
orchestration.driver_expectation: a driver loop calls the phase methods in turn_order's order for active_faction each turn, calling advance_phase() between them, then calls process_game_end_check and only calls advance_turn() if GameState.game_over is still False afterward (advance_turn() raises if the game is already over -- process_game_end_check may have just set it). It must also be phase-aware (see game_start_settings.driver_implication), since advance_phase() may skip a phase the driver would otherwise unconditionally call into. See engine/tests/test_engine.py's TestFullTurnLoopIntegration for a worked example with empty/trivial orders (proving the orchestration itself holds up over multiple turns and factions), and engine/bots/driver.py's play_to_completion for a real, phase-aware bot-driven driver loop.

turn_order.summary: Spend the faction's treasury_mpc budget and choose deploy locations. The units are decided now but don't appear on the board yet -- they sit in TerritoryState.pending_deployment until Deploy + Income.

Units move to attack; every combat move must result in an attack -- relocating a unit into the target territory/sea zone is what makes it contested (see movement.combat_move_destination). No separate 'declare an attack from next door' step. Implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.submit_combat_moves/confirm_combat_moves and movement.trace_combat_move.
execution_notes: Orders carry a full PATH (origin through destination, every consecutive pair adjacent), not just a destination -- a Mechanized Infantry blitz can enter more than one undefended foreign territory in a single move, and knowing which ones requires the actual route, since a unit can have more than one equal-length legal route to the same endpoint.

Every enemy LAND territory entered or merely passed through is marked contested -- confirmed this session: even an entirely undefended Mechanized Infantry blitz never captures outright, regardless of whether anyone was defending it or the unit just kept moving. Ownership is resolved LATER, in Capture Territory, from whatever the board looks like by then (after Combat Resolution AND Non-Combat Move have both had their say) -- this is a real change from an earlier version of this session's design, which had an uncontested capture apply immediately at Combat Move time; that's no longer how it works.

Orders in one submission are executed IN ORDER, each against the board as already mutated by the earlier ones -- so a later order can see contested state an earlier order just created within the same submission (e.g. two units converging on the same territory). validate (submit_combat_moves) and commit (confirm_combat_moves) both run the identical sequence, submit against a throwaway deep copy purely to check it, confirm against the real GameState.

Air units supply a 2-entry [origin, destination] path (no hop-by-hop legality or capture concerns) and validate against movement.legal_air_move_destinations instead of trace_combat_move; an air combat move always marks the destination contested, never captures (air alone can't capture).

Moving an Aircraft Carrier sweeps along embarked aircraft too (carrier_air_operations.carrier_ride_along) -- they become real combatants in the resulting battle for free, since gather_battle_units only cares about physical presence.

turn_order.summary: Every declared sea battle resolves to completion first, then every declared land battle (combat.battle_resolution_pass_order) -- never interleaved. Each battle: an air-superiority round if triggered, then up to 3 main rounds. Not reversible once started -- no mid-battle retreat, dice already rolled. Implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.resolve_combat/declared_battles/gather_battle_units.
execution_notes: declared_battles(faction) is every contested territory where faction currently has units present -- covers a fresh attack from this same turn's Combat Move AND a standing multi-turn stalemate faction is still part of (combat.multi_party_battles.attacker_always_solo: a faction's units only ever fight during THAT faction's own Combat Resolution, so an old stalemate gets refought whenever its attacker's turn comes back around, never on someone else's).

gather_battle_units is a pure query (no mutation) exposed separately from the auto-play resolve_combat, so a future interactive UI can call it directly to build its own combat.resolve_battle() generator for step-by-step play instead of only getting the auto-played result.

After each battle: dead units (from BattleEvent's eliminated_*_ids) are removed from the territory; then the CLAIMING check (combat.contested_territory_rule's claiming update, this session) -- if the attacking faction and its current allies have NO land or sea unit left in the territory at all (air alone never counts -- same standard as Capture Territory's 'air can't capture'), contested_by clears IMMEDIATELY, whatever the battle's own outcome was, including a 3-round stalemate the attacker's ground/naval force didn't survive while the defender's did. No longer contested also means no longer a legal non-combat-move destination for anyone else (movement.noncombat_move_destination never allows a clean, non-allied foreign territory). Otherwise (the attacking coalition still has ground/naval presence): for a LAND territory, contested_by is left exactly as it is regardless of outcome -- even a decisive win -- since Capture Territory (a later phase, not here) is what actually resolves a won attack into an ownership change, from the board state this leaves behind; for a SEA zone (no Capture-Territory equivalent to defer to), contested_by clears on any decisive outcome (attacker_eliminated / defender_eliminated / mutual_elimination) same as before, and stays set only for an unresolved 3-round stalemate, refought next time declared_battles picks it up. A real bug existed here before this session's fix: contested_by used to clear unconditionally on every decisive outcome, including a decisive LAND win with the attacker's own unit still standing there -- which silently broke Capture Territory's `faction in t.contested_by` gate and meant a won attack's ownership never actually flipped except via the unrelated Mechanized-Infantry-blitz-through-empty-territory path.

round1_bonus_side IS determined here now (all three combat.first_round_bonuses cases are fully implemented) -- see resolve_combat's own docstring for the exact priority order: former-ally reclaim (recurring, attacker or defender role, combat.true_territory_loss.betrayal_exception), sea-deploy ambush, then amphibious landing.

Sea battles run combat.emergency_landing's check after every battle regardless of outcome: any surviving DEFENDING aircraft left without their own faction's carrier get find_emergency_landing's one-hop search, scoped per-owner since defenders can be pooled across several factions and each only cares about its own carrier. Attacking aircraft are untouched (defender only, per that rule).

turn_order.summary: Units that didn't combat-move this turn may reposition. Air units are exempt from the combat-move/non-combat-move exclusivity that binds everyone else -- they can always non-combat-move too, even after already attacking. Implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.submit_noncombat_moves/confirm_noncombat_moves.
execution_notes: Entering a territory the mover is already contesting -- or one contested by any other factions entirely, unrelated to the mover -- is simply a legal destination (movement.noncombat_move_destination), no different from any other legal move (confirmed this session, and already how legal_noncombat_move_destinations was built). No contested_by bookkeeping happens here at all: a newly-arrived unit is picked up automatically by the next Combat Resolution pass through gather_battle_units, which only checks who's physically PRESENT, never how they got there.

Orders carry just a destination, not a path like CombatMoveOrder does -- there's no capture/blitz concept for a non-combat move, so only the endpoint matters; legal_noncombat_move_destinations/legal_air_move_destinations already do their own BFS internally.

carrier_air_operations is now fully wired in for this phase: process_return_to_base runs first (an automated, non-staged step -- see that entry), and carrier_ride_along fires automatically whenever a NonCombatMoveOrder moves an Aircraft Carrier. movement.stranded_aircraft_rule then runs as confirm_noncombat_moves' last step. carrier_ride_along for a COMBAT move (a carrier attacking with embarked aircraft as combatants) is still not implemented -- see that entry's status.

turn_order.summary: Automatic, derived from the WHOLE turn's outcomes -- Combat Move (which territories were entered/passed through, now marked contested), Combat Resolution (who's still standing), and Non-Combat Move (any reinforcements that arrived after the fighting). For every territory the active faction is contesting where no non-allied LAND units remain present, awards it to whichever of the active faction or its allies actually holds the ground (see capture_winner_rule below) -- covers an undefended entry nobody ever fought over, a battle won outright even if the loser's only survivors are air units (air can't hold ground), AND the case where the active faction's own land presence was wiped out but an ally's wasn't. Leaves ownership untouched, even for a since-eliminated original owner, as long as a genuine contest between two or more factions OTHER than the active faction/its allies is still live (see combat.contested_territory_rule). Air units alone can never capture (no ground presence, nothing to hold the territory) -- no player choice here, nothing to roll back. Implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.process_capture_territory.

capture_winner_rule.rule: the active faction wins if it has even a single land unit present, no matter how few ('if you have one land unit, you can keep it') -- an ally's presence never blocks this. Only when the active faction has ZERO land units left in a territory it's contesting does the claim pass to an ally: among faction's allies who DO have land units present, the one with the greatest TOTAL cost (units.json's cost field, summed across all its land units in that territory) wins; ties broken by turn order (earlier wins). If literally nobody -- not the active faction, not any ally -- has land units present (it simply passed through and kept moving), the active faction still gets the claim by default, since no ally has any better claim either.
capture_winner_rule.confirmed_this_session: this scenario -- your land units all eliminated during your own turn, but an ally's still present -- awards the territory to the ally, even though it's still your own Capture Territory phase doing the awarding, not the ally's.
capture_winner_rule.turn_order_definition: GameState.factions' fixed iteration order (inferred, not independently confirmed with the user -- flag before relying on it if the actual intended meaning turns out to be something more dynamic, like 'whichever ally's turn comes up next in the rotation from this point')

turn_order.summary: Purchase's pending_deployment units actually appear on the board now (applying purchase's carrierless-air and lost-contested-purchase fallbacks, and marking a hostile sea deploy contested). Income is collected for next turn's budget, then the global recovery/heal check runs over the WHOLE board (every faction's units, not just the active one's) -- see combat.recovery_rule. Automatic -- no player choice, nothing to roll back.

A faction may optionally invite_to_alliance or withdraw_from_alliance -- one action per faction per turn (see alliances.alliances_phase_action). No longer a no-op stub: fully implemented, including the Strategic-Center withdrawal lock, the rejoin ban, and the former-ally reclaim bonus setup. There is no special end-of-game withdrawal window here -- victory.game_end_rule's check runs AFTER this phase's regular action, see alliances.withdraw_from_alliance.no_special_end_of_game_window.

multi_party_battles.attacker_always_solo: the attacking side of any battle is always exactly one faction's units -- the currently active faction's, and only its own. Allies never combine their units into one attacking side, even if an ally's units happen to already be sitting at the same contested destination (from their own earlier turn) -- each faction's units only ever fight in the resolve_battle() call that happens during THAT faction's own Combat Resolution phase, never pooled with another faction's units into a single battle regardless of the scenario.
multi_party_battles.defenders_pool_together: the defending side is every unit present belonging to ANY faction that is not an ally of the attacker, pooled into ONE side for a single resolve_battle() call -- regardless of how many distinct non-allied factions that represents, and regardless of whether those factions are themselves allied with each other or are enemies of each other. There is no picking a single target faction among several non-allied factions present (supersedes the older design-doc idea that the attacker chooses which one to fight -- see alliances.design_doc_reference's note).
multi_party_battles.why_no_combat_py_changes_were_needed: combat.py's resolve_battle() never reads UnitInstance.owner at all -- target selection, weighting, and damage are entirely unit_type/stats-based -- so a pooled multi-faction defender_units list already works correctly with zero changes to combat.py itself. This rule is entirely about how the Combat Resolution phase must GATHER attacker_units/defender_units before calling resolve_battle(): attacker_units = the active faction's units at that location; defender_units = every OTHER unit there whose owner isn't an ally of the active faction, regardless of how many distinct owners that covers.
multi_party_battles.status: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.gather_battle_units, which builds attacker_units/defender_units exactly this way for every call into combat.resolve_battle().

combat.air_superiority_trigger: occurs only if both sides in the battle have at least 1 air unit present AND at least one of the two sides has at least 1 Fighter present; two bomber-only air forces facing each other do not trigger it

air_superiority_die_adjustments.fighter: attack die steps up TWO sizes for this round only (D6 -> D10, the design doc's "D10 Attack"), stacking on top of an existing promotion the same way first_round_bonuses would (a promoted Fighter, D6->D8 from promotion, steps to D12 for air superiority).
air_superiority_die_adjustments.bomber: attack die is unchanged (its base D8 already is the design doc's "D8 Attack"; a promoted Bomber keeps its promotion die), and damage is fixed at 2 for this round -- an absolute override of Bomber's normal 3, not a relative one (promotion doesn't touch damage either, so there's nothing to stack against here). Before the design doc's aircraft die/damage reduction this was a one-size step DOWN (D10 -> D8); with the base die now D8 the step is gone.
air_superiority_die_adjustments.scope: only the pre-combat air-superiority round (round_number 0) -- rounds 1-3 of main combat use each unit's normal stats. Never touches defense, only the acting unit's own die/damage.

combat.hit_rule: attack die roll >= target's defense is a hit; the max value on the die always hits, even against a target whose defense exceeds the roll
combat.damage_rule: a hit deals damage equal to the attacker's damage rating. A target normally reachable by the roll (defense <= roll) is always preferred and takes full damage, even if the roll happens to be the die's max value. The max-die-always-hits bypass -- reaching a target whose defense exceeds the roll -- is only used once no normally-reachable target remains, and even then is restricted to the single next-highest defense tier above the roll (see target_selection.fallback_rule; a tougher tier still is never reached), and that bypass hit specifically deals half damage (rounded down): the cost of forcing a hit on an otherwise-unhittable target, not a tax on rolling well.

resolution_order.note: within a round, each side resolves its own units grouped by type in this fixed order, then by attack die size ascending within a type (promotions can give same-type units different dice). Same order applies to attacker and defender.

target_selection.eligible_pool_rule: enemy units in the battle with defense <= the attack roll and HP > 0 (not yet eliminated this round)
target_selection.fallback_rule: if the eligible pool is empty, fall back to the eligible units with the next-lowest defense above the roll. This same fallback pool is what a max-die bypass hit draws from too, not the full standing roster -- a unit whose defense is even higher (a tougher tier still) is excluded either way.
target_selection.weighting_note: an attacking unit is twice as likely to target an eligible enemy unit of its own unit type as any other eligible unit, except a Bomber attacker, which uses uniform (1x) weighting across the whole eligible pool. Bombers themselves are ordinary targets for everyone else's attacks -- no special protection, no extra likelihood.

submarine_air_invisibility.rule: a Submarine attacker's target pool never includes an Air-category unit (Fighter, Bomber), and an Air-category attacker's target pool never includes a Submarine -- excluded entirely before the eligible/fallback pool logic runs, regardless of the roll (even the max-die bypass, which can otherwise reach a target whose defense exceeds the roll, can never reach one). If that exclusion (or the enemy having no one left standing) leaves a unit with no legal target, that unit does not roll at all -- no die is spent, and the battle log says so with a NO_TARGETS event -- checked as each unit's turn comes, so hits earlier in the same roll-through count. And a round is not fought when neither side has any unit with a legal target (e.g. only Submarines against only aircraft): the battle ends there, still contested, with BATTLE_END end_reason 'no_targets'.
submarine_air_invisibility.source: units.json's 'Submerge' special ability ("can't engage or be attacked by aircraft")

combat.casualty_resolution: attacker rolls all attacks first (defending casualties noted, not removed), then defender rolls all attacks (both sides' casualties removed together)
combat.progressive_elimination_note: within one side's own ordered roll-through (per resolution_order), damage accumulates progressively against the other side -- a unit-type group resolving later in that same side's sequence can find its preferred targets already reduced to 0 HP by an earlier group in the sequence. Actual removal from the board for BOTH sides happens together only after both attacker and defender have finished rolling for the round.
combat.battle_resolution_pass_note: global across the whole map for a turn's combat resolution step -- every declared sea battle resolves to completion first, then every declared land battle; never interleaved per battle pair. This is what allows surviving transports/escorts from an already-resolved naval battle to continue their combat move into the adjacent land battle before it resolves.
combat.promotion_check_note: promotion is checked after every round of combat, including the air-superiority round -- a mid-battle promotion (die size up, +1 defense) affects that same battle's remaining rounds.
combat.recovery_rule: a unit heals to full HP once a full round has elapsed since it last took part in a round of combat, counting the turn it was hurt on as the start of that count. Tracked against a single global, monotonically-increasing turn counter (one tick per faction-turn, not per round): a unit heals once current_global_turn - last_combat_global_turn >= num_factions, checked at the deploy phase of EVERY faction's turn, over the whole board -- not only the acting faction's own units. Example: a unit damaged during faction X's turn heals at the deploy phase of faction X's NEXT turn (exactly one full round later), provided it hasn't been in combat again since.
combat.contested_territory_rule: if units remain on both sides after 3 rounds, the territory stays with its original owner, contributes no MPC to either side, and only the owner's Infantry may be mustered there until resolved. Even if the registered owner has since been eliminated from the game entirely, ownership is maintained exactly as it stands as long as two (or more) OTHER factions are still genuinely contesting the territory -- elimination of the nominal owner doesn't itself trigger any reassignment; see turn_order's Capture Territory entry for how a contest actually resolves once it's down to one faction's land units.
combat.claiming_update: if, after Combat Resolution, the attacking faction and its current allies have no LAND or SEA unit left in a territory at all (air alone never holds a claim -- same standard as 'air can't capture'), that territory is IMMEDIATELY no longer contested -- not just at the later Capture Territory phase. This also makes it ineligible as a non-combat-move destination for anyone else (movement.noncombat_move_destination never allows a clean, non-allied foreign territory). See turn_order's Combat Resolution execution_notes for the full rule, including how this differs for land (contested_by otherwise stays set through a decisive win, pending Capture Territory) versus sea (no Capture-Territory equivalent, so it clears on any decisive outcome once the attacking side still has presence). Implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine._apply_battle_outcome/_attacking_coalition_has_ground_or_naval_presence. NEW this session -- see combat.true_territory_loss: if the territory the attacking coalition just lost all presence in was the ACTIVE faction's own registered land holding (attacker_always_solo labels a faction 'attacker' even when it's really just defending its own ground against a standing contest), the surviving non-allied side actually takes ownership right here, immediately -- not left to Capture Territory, which would never revisit this territory once it's no longer listed in contested_by.

true_territory_loss.trigger: the active faction's own Combat Resolution phase re-fights a standing contest against its OWN registered land territory (an enemy attacked it on an earlier turn and the 3-round stalemate carried over) -- attacker_always_solo means the engine labels the active faction 'attacker' for this battle regardless of the narrative (it's genuinely defending, not attacking). Confirmed by the user this session: 'the clearest path to being eliminated on your turn is an enemy contesting your SC. You need to fight back (or withdraw) during your turn. Your forces might lose... this can lead to a true loss of territory' -- and it applies to any contested land territory the active faction owns, not just Strategic Centers, and needs no ally involved at all (a related but separate ally-claims-it case already existed in _determine_capture_winner, for when process_capture_territory awards a WON attack to an ally instead of the active faction itself -- this is the mirror image: a LOST defense handing the active faction's own ground to the enemy).
true_territory_loss.effect: if the active faction's coalition ends the battle with zero LAND or SEA presence in a territory IT OWNS (combat.claiming_update's trigger, land battles only -- sea zones have no ownership), the surviving non-allied side takes ownership immediately, at the end of combat resolution -- not deferred to Capture Territory, which only ever scans territories the active faction is STILL listed in contested_by for, and this is exactly what just got cleared. Recorded as an ordinary capture in GameStats (same Territory Captures report entry a normal win produces), attributed to the new owner, not the active faction whose turn it happened on.
true_territory_loss.winner_among_multiple_non_allies: combat.multi_party_battles can pool more than one distinct non-allied faction onto the defending side of a single battle -- whichever of them has the greatest TOTAL cost of land units left in the territory wins it; ties broken by turn order (GameState.factions' fixed iteration order, earlier wins). Same tie-break formula _determine_capture_winner uses among allies, just applied among non-allies here instead.
true_territory_loss.no_winner_case: if NOBODY has land presence left (a mutual wipe, or only air survives on either side -- air alone never holds a claim, same standard as everywhere else), the ground is simply abandoned, not captured: ownership stays with the active faction by default, and this is reported as an ordinary contest-ended-without-capture, not a capture.
true_territory_loss.status: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine._apply_battle_outcome/_true_territory_loss_winner (the core rule and its betrayal_exception) and process_capture_territory/withdraw_from_alliance (where TerritoryState.reclaim_bonus_for is set and, once the contest resolves, cleared).
true_territory_loss.betrayal_exception: Confirmed by the user this session: "having troops on enemy lands is an exception to transferring ownership... In cases of betrayal, the contestation can only be cleared during the betrayer's claim territory phase. Until then, the original owner can marshal infantry there, do both combat and non-combat moves into the territory, gets the first round combat bonus on attack and defense in the territory." Concretely: this whole true_territory_loss mechanism is SKIPPED (no ownership change, contested_by left completely untouched) whenever the territory's TerritoryState.reclaim_bonus_for still names the active faction -- an alliance-betrayal reclaim in progress. The original owner keeps getting fresh chances (each with the recurring first_round_bonuses reclaim bonus) across as many of its own turns as it takes; the betrayer can only actually finish claiming the ground via the ORDINARY process_capture_territory path, on the betrayer's own Capture Territory phase, once the original owner has zero presence there at that exact moment. Marching new Infantry into the contested territory (purchase.contested_land_deploy_restriction already allows Infantry into any contested territory generally, not a betrayal-specific carve-out) and moving there via combat OR non-combat move (movement.combat_move_destination's join_contest / movement.noncombat_move_destination's own-or-contested rule, both already general) are unaffected by any of this -- already legal before this session, for any contested territory the mover owns or is allied to.

dig_in.effect: +1 defense (capped at 10), every round of a battle (not round-1-only) -- unlike first_round_bonuses below, this is unconditional and entirely intrinsic to combat.py: it applies automatically whenever a unit with the trait is on the defending side, with no engine.py-level trigger determination needed.
dig_in.which_units: data-driven from units.json's special_abilities (a string starting with 'Dig In') rather than a hardcoded unit-type check -- currently Infantry only, but any future unit type tagged the same way picks it up automatically. See UnitInstance.effective_stats' `defending` parameter in engine/state.py.
dig_in.stacking: additive with promotion and, in round 1 specifically, first_round_bonuses -- a promoted, Dig-In-equipped Infantry defending in a round-1 battle that also qualifies for a first_round_bonus gets all three defense bonuses at once (still capped at 10).

first_round_bonuses.magnitude: attack die steps up one size (max D12) and +1 defense (max 10) -- the same transform a promotion applies, but temporary and not persisted: it's recomputed fresh every relevant call, applies only to round_number == 1 of main combat (never the air-superiority round, never rounds 2-3), and grants no HP (unlike promotion's +1 HP). Stacks additively with an existing promotion -- a promoted unit that also qualifies steps its die up twice and gets +2 defense, still capped at D12/10, for that one round.
first_round_bonuses.mechanism_status: implemented -- resolve_battle() takes an optional round1_bonus_side ('attacker' | 'defender' | None, default None) and applies it via UnitInstance.effective_stats(unit_defs, round1_bonus=True) to every unit on that side. All three cases below are now fully wired end-to-end in GameEngine.resolve_combat, in priority order when more than one could theoretically apply to the same battle (never happens in practice, since reclaim/amphibious are land-only and ambush is sea-only, but the order is: reclaim, then ambush, then amphibious).

cases.name: amphibious landing
cases.trigger: the attack is a pure amphibious assault THIS TURN -- every Land-category unit on the attacking side both combat-moved this turn (UnitInstance.has_moved_combat) and did so via a path that touched a sea zone (UnitInstance.arrived_amphibiously, stamped from movement.trace_combat_move's crossed_water). Negated entirely (no bonus at all, for either side) if even one attacking land unit reached the battle overland instead, or if any attacking land unit is simply STANDING THERE from an earlier turn without moving again this turn (a multi-turn stalemate refought without a fresh combat move never qualifies, even if the same units are still sitting there) -- confirmed this session: the bonus is one-shot, tied to the turn the landing actually happens, not a persistent 'hasn't walked since' tracker. Never applies with zero land attackers present (not vacuously true) or to a sea battle.
cases.status: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine._execute_combat_moves (stamps arrived_amphibiously on every land unit's own combat move), GameEngine.advance_turn (resets it alongside has_moved_combat at the end of that unit owner's turn), GameEngine.resolve_combat (the actual check, land battles only), and movement.CombatMoveTrace.crossed_water (the underlying did-this-path-touch-a-sea-zone signal, already computed internally by trace_combat_move for the water movement-budget bonus, just newly exposed).

cases.name: sea deploy into enemy-occupied zone
cases.trigger: a faction deploys new sea units directly into a sea zone occupied by a non-ally -- legal, since sea zones have no ownership/occupation-blocks-deploy concept the way land does, and Deploy happens after that turn's combat resolution, so no battle results from the deploy itself. The zone becomes CONTESTED immediately as a direct result of the deployment (see purchase.hostile_sea_deploy_creates_contested) -- not silent co-occupation. When the prior occupant then makes a combat move to attack (joining/resolving that contested zone) on their own later turn, they get the bonus -- catching the freshly-deployed fleet unprepared. The bonus belongs to whoever was already sitting there when the deploy happened, not the depositing faction. If more than one distinct non-allied faction already shares the zone when the hostile deploy lands, EVERY one of them is queued independently -- confirmed this session: each was equally caught unprepared, not just whichever was there first.
cases.status: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine._deploy_to_sea (marks the zone contested AND queues every prior non-ally into TerritoryState.ambush_bonus_for, a set supporting more than one simultaneous claimant) and GameEngine.resolve_combat (grants the bonus and removes just that one faction from the set on their own next attack there -- any other still-queued faction's entry is untouched).

cases.name: former-ally territory reclaim
cases.recipient: the betrayed former ally -- as ATTACKER on its own turn, or as DEFENDER if the betrayer attacks it there instead (confirmed this session, a broadening from the original attacker-only design)
cases.trigger: an alliance breaks and one member is left occupying territory that used to belong to the other; the original owner gets the bonus retaking it. RECURRING (changed this session from the original one-shot design): the bonus re-applies every qualifying battle here, for as long as TerritoryState.reclaim_bonus_for stays set -- it is NOT cleared just because one attempt happened to fail. See combat.true_territory_loss's betrayal_exception for why: a single failed counter-attack must not hand the original owner's own territory to the betrayer.
cases.status: implemented -- see alliances.withdraw_from_alliance's reclaim_setup and TerritoryState.reclaim_bonus_for; GameEngine.resolve_combat reads it (attacker OR defender role) every relevant battle, and only GameEngine.process_capture_territory (or _apply_battle_outcome, if the betrayer's own attack fails outright) ever clears it, once the contest is genuinely resolved.

emergency_landing.trigger: a defending Aircraft Carrier is destroyed during a sea battle, stranding surviving aircraft that were relying on it
emergency_landing.timing: resolved ONLY once the whole battle has concluded (win, loss, or contested after the 3-round cap) -- never mid-battle. An aircraft whose carrier is destroyed in, say, round 1 of a 3-round battle keeps fighting normally through every remaining round of that same battle exactly as if nothing had happened to its carrier; only after the battle fully resolves does this rule check whether any defending aircraft are left in a sea zone with no own carrier surviving.
emergency_landing.scope: defender only. An attacker whose carrier is destroyed mid-battle has no equivalent rescue -- its stranded aircraft are simply lost with no emergency-landing search.
emergency_landing.search: a one-hop search of the battle sea zone's adjacent territories (engine/movement.py's find_emergency_landing), not bounded by the aircraft's own move budget. Priority: an adjacent own carrier first, then adjacent own land, then adjacent allied land -- notably NOT an ally's carrier, which (unlike a voluntary non-combat landing declaration) is not treated as a safe home for a forced landing. Random choice among tied options within the same priority tier. If nothing qualifies, the aircraft is lost.
emergency_landing.engine_note: find_emergency_landing itself is a pure spatial query with no opinion on when it should be called -- enforcing the timing (post-battle only) and scope (defender only) described above is engine.py's job, not movement.py's.
emergency_landing.status: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine._resolve_stranded_defender_aircraft, called once per sea battle after _apply_battle_outcome removes the dead.

transport_form_in_sea_battles.rule: in a SEA battle every Land-category unit present (either side) is Transport cargo for that battle: it cannot attack (no attack die), has the Transport's stats from units.json (defense 6, 1 HP), earns no XP and cannot be promoted, and is eliminated by any single hit -- the cargo is lost with its ship. A cargo unit that survives gets its own HP back afterwards (transport damage never carries over to the land unit).
transport_form_in_sea_battles.scope: sea battles only; the same unit fights normally in a land battle. A round-1 combat bonus still adds +1 to its (Transport) defense; Dig In and promotion do not apply while in transport form.
transport_form_in_sea_battles.status: implemented -- see UnitInstance.in_transport_form / effective_stats and combat.resolve_battle. Before this the engine let land units fight at sea with their own dice, defense and HP, contradicting movement.transport_amphibious and this file's own transport notes.

movement.combat_move_destination: a combat move physically relocates the attacking units into the target territory/sea zone, which is what makes it contested -- there is no separate 'declare attack from next door' step. Every enemy LAND territory entered or merely passed through this way is marked contested -- confirmed this session: even an entirely undefended Mechanized Infantry blitz never captures outright the moment it passes through (or stops), regardless of whether anyone was defending it. Ownership is resolved later, in the Capture Territory phase, from whatever the board looks like by then -- see that phase's entry and combat.multi_party_battles' neighbor, the Capture Territory logic.
movement.no_mid_battle_retreat: once combat starts resolving there is no retreat: a battle ends in elimination of one side, the defender holding after 3 rounds if the attacker is wiped, or the territory becoming contested after 3 rounds if both sides still have units
movement.contested_land_combat_move_rule: a land unit sitting in an already-contested LAND territory may combat-move to another already-contested land space (press the fight elsewhere), or retreat to a friendly (own or allied) space, but may NOT use a combat move to stage a fresh attack from there into a not-yet-contested enemy space -- that must originate from an uncontested friendly space. Land you own (or an ally owns) that is currently contested IS a legal combat-move destination for land, sea-borne and air units alike -- you join the fight for it (and may pass on through it like any own land); uncontested own land is not (nothing to attack). This is a land-only concept: sea zones are never owned/controlled by a faction the way land is, so a sea unit leaving a sea zone where a battle just happened moves under the ordinary combat-move rules, unrestricted.
movement.enemy_occupation_stop_rule: a land or sea combat move that enters a territory/sea zone occupied by a NON-ALLY (i.e. has non-allied defending units present) must stop there -- it cannot chain through to a further destination in the same move. Own and allied territory is always freely transitable regardless of contested status. Transports never count as an occupying presence for this check (a zone with only enemy Transports in it doesn't block passage, combat or non-combat, and doesn't force a stop); a Transport is any land unit afloat in a sea zone (there is no separate Transport unit on the board), and it can still be attacked by ending a combat move (or an air combat move) in its zone. Air units are exempt entirely and may fly over enemy-held territory freely, in either the combat-move or non-combat-move phase -- EXCEPT an enemy Fighter specifically, which disrupts that freedom; see air_interception_rule.
movement.empty_foreign_territory_rule: a combat move CAN pass through an empty (undefended) foreign land territory rather than stopping there -- but only Mechanized Infantry has this ability; every other LAND unit type stops upon entering ANY foreign territory, empty or occupied, same as the enemy_occupation_stop_rule (sea units never enter land at all -- see sea_units_stay_at_sea). Mechanized Infantry itself still stops on an OCCUPIED foreign territory as normal -- the exception is for empty ones only, and is bounded by its own remaining move budget like any other move, not a separately-limited ability. Passing through marks it contested (combat_move_destination), not captured -- the actual claim is Capture Territory's job.
movement.noncombat_move_destination: own or allied territory (contested or not -- always legal for land/sea pass-through and stopping), or any territory already contested regardless of who owns it or who's contesting it (unqualified -- not limited to the mover's own contest). Never a clean (uncontested), non-allied foreign land territory. A sea zone occupied by a non-ally blocks non-combat movement entirely (that would require a combat move instead) -- enemy Transports alone do not count as occupying -- an allied warship's presence does not. Air units follow a different, stricter landing rule -- see air_landing_rule.
movement.air_landing_rule: a non-combat air move must end on own-or-allied land (contested or not -- landing there doesn't care about contested status either way, unlike ground pass-through rules) or specifically the mover's OWN aircraft carrier -- never an ally's carrier, even though an ally's land is fine, and that own-only standard for a carrier holds regardless of contested status too (confirmed this session: the restriction has only ever been on the sea/carrier side, never on land -- allied land, contested or not, stays a legal landing spot). That own carrier may already be sitting there, or merely queued in this turn's pending_deployment -- see carrier_air_operations.open_water_anticipation for exactly what does and doesn't count. A combat air move must end on a real attack target -- non-ally-occupied territory, or already contested (joining the fight) -- own/allied territory isn't an attack, and neither is empty foreign territory, since air alone can't capture (per turn_order's Capture Territory phase); there's nothing there to actually attack.
movement.air_interception_rule: aircraft generally fly over enemy AND neutral territories/sea zones (including enemy land and sea units) freely in both combat and non-combat moves, without provoking an attack or being blocked -- neutral_exclusion's 'not enterable, not attackable' still applies to LANDING or ATTACKING there, just not to merely passing over. The sole exception is an enemy FIGHTER specifically (never a Bomber, never any other unit type, and never simple non-ally/neutral presence alone) physically present in a territory/sea zone the path would enter or pass through -- 'enemy' meaning belonging to a faction that is neither the mover nor one of its allies. Where an enemy Fighter is present: a combat move is forced to stop there and attack, exactly like ordinary enemy occupation does for land/sea units (enemy_occupation_stop_rule) -- it cannot continue past it to a further destination in the same move; a non-combat move may neither land there nor pass through it at all -- that territory/sea zone is entirely off limits for the rest of that move. Not checked by carrier_air_operations.return_to_base_after_combat's automatic snap-back -- that is a direct return to a recorded origin, not a fresh pathfinding move, so there is no path to intercept. Implemented -- see engine.movement.legal_air_move_destinations and its _enemy_fighter_present helper.
movement.combat_or_noncombat_not_both: non-air units (land and sea) may combat-move OR non-combat-move in a turn, never both. Air units are the sole exception and may always make a non-combat move too, even after already making a combat move the same turn -- the two aren't mutually exclusive for air the way they are for everyone else.
movement.alliance_note: FactionState.alliance (see alliances section below) is now actively consulted by movement legality -- own-or-allied territory/units are treated as friendly/non-blocking throughout this section -- even though full alliance MECHANICS (joining, withdrawing, betrayal, the reclaim bonus) remain out of scope for v1. See alliances.status.
movement.water_movement_bonus_rule: a land unit that begins its turn in a sea zone, OR enters a sea zone at any point during its current move (becoming Transport cargo -- one transport per unit), gets a flat +1 added to BOTH its combat_move and non_combat_move stat for the rest of that turn. This applies dynamically/retroactively: as soon as the unit touches water mid-move, its remaining hop budget for the move in progress extends by 1 -- e.g. Infantry (combat_move 1) can combat-move onto adjacent water then continue onto adjacent land, because entering the water grants the +1 that pays for the second hop. A Mechanized Infantry that begins its turn already in water can move 3 spaces that turn (base 2 + 1). There is no separate per-hop cost to board or disembark -- this flat bonus is the whole model.
movement.transport_amphibious: surviving transports (and the land units they carry) can continue a combat move into adjacent land after winning/surviving the naval battle, only possible because sea battles resolve before land battles (see combat.battle_resolution_pass_order). A transported unit's Transport is destroyed with it if sunk. Transported units don't earn XP. A land unit in transit may move THROUGH a HOSTILE sea zone -- one that's either occupied (enemy combatants present) or already contested (an unresolved battle there) -- specifically to reach adjacent land, but not to chain onward into a further, more open sea zone beyond that. The land reached this way can be enemy territory (an attack), an empty foreign territory (a capture), a territory already contested (joining the fight), OR the mover's own friendly territory (landing safely to escape the hostile water) -- landing is always a legal way to end the move regardless of whose land it is, and it's still classified as a combat move even when it ends on friendly soil, since it's the act of crossing hostile water that requires one, not the destination. Completing the crossing is contingent on the unit surviving that sea zone's naval battle first, since it lands only after the battle resolves, not before or regardless of the outcome.
movement.sea_units_stay_at_sea: a SEA unit (category 'Sea': Submarine, Cruiser, Aircraft Carrier, and the Transport wrapper) never leaves the water, in either move phase: it can never end a move on land, pass over a land territory (land is not a bridge between two sea zones), or attack land. Enforced in engine.movement._reachable_destinations (so legal_combat_move_destinations/legal_noncombat_move_destinations and every _paths variant, and through them the bots and the client's legal-option lists) and again in trace_combat_move, which validates the exact path of a submitted order, so a hand-built order onto land is rejected too. Land units riding a Transport through water are unaffected (that's the water_movement_bonus_rule / transport_amphibious case, and it is the land unit that lands, never the ship). Purchases were already guarded: a sea unit cannot be bought onto a land territory. Added after bot ships were observed ending combat moves on -- and fighting from -- land territories, because the reachability search had no land restriction for sea units at all.
movement.neutral_exclusion: NEUTRAL territories are excluded from every legal move/attack target entirely -- not enterable, not attackable. The sole exception is air overflight: an aircraft may freely pass THROUGH a neutral territory/sea zone en route to a further destination (see air_interception_rule) -- it still can never land there or attack it.
movement.stranded_aircraft_rule: if the Non-Combat Move phase ends with an aircraft sitting over a sea zone with no OWN carrier present (an ally's carrier does not count), that aircraft is lost. This is a phase-end consequence, not a move-legality rule; it runs once, after the whole non-combat-move phase resolves. A client UI is expected to warn a player before letting them end the phase with aircraft stranded this way, but that warning is the client's job, not the engine's -- the engine only enforces the actual loss. In practice this now mostly matters for carrier_air_operations' return-to-base and ride-along cases below, since open_water_anticipation already makes it illegal to knowingly DECLARE a move that would leave an aircraft stranded with no own carrier at all. Implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine._apply_stranded_aircraft_check, run automatically as the last step of confirm_noncombat_moves.

carrier_air_operations.scope: all of the rules below apply to the ACTIVE player's own turn only -- their own aircraft, during their own Combat Move / Combat Resolution / Non-Combat Move phases. A DEFENDING faction never moves (it isn't their turn), so none of this applies to a defender's aircraft; a defender's aircraft whose carrier is destroyed mid-battle remains governed entirely by combat.emergency_landing (unchanged by any of this -- still defender-only, still forced, still resolved only once that battle ends).

return_to_base_after_combat.rule: surviving air units that made a combat move (attacked) return automatically to their start-of-turn location once combat resolves -- if that location was a carrier, they return to that SAME carrier wherever it currently is (which may already have moved earlier the same turn, e.g. if the carrier itself made a combat move). This automatic return REPLACES the unit's non-combat move for the turn -- not optional, and not on top of a separately-chosen non-combat move.
return_to_base_after_combat.exception: if the unit's start-of-turn carrier or territory is itself lost (destroyed or captured) during this same combat phase, the automatic return has nowhere to go -- the unit instead gets an ordinary non-combat move (its real move budget, normal legal_air_move_destinations rules, no special priority list) to find a landing spot.
return_to_base_after_combat.status: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.process_return_to_base, an automated step callers must run at the very start of the Non-Combat Move phase, before submit_noncombat_moves (which refuses to run until it has). UnitInstance.combat_move_origin/based_on_carrier, stamped by _execute_combat_moves on every air unit's combat move, record where to send it back to; both are cleared once process_return_to_base consumes them. A LAND origin becoming invalid never actually happens under currently-implemented rules (nobody else acts on the active faction's own turn, so their own land can't change hands mid-turn) -- the exception mostly bites the carrier case, when the carrier itself was part of this turn's attack and didn't survive it.

carrier_ride_along.rule: an air unit currently based on a carrier (UnitInstance.based_on_carrier) moves WITH that carrier by default when the carrier moves -- this counts as the air unit's own combat or non-combat move, matching whichever type the carrier made (a carrier combat-moving into an attack carries its embarked aircraft into that same battle as combatants; a non-combat move just repositions them together).
carrier_ride_along.preemption: the air unit can instead make its OWN independent non-combat move before the carrier moves this phase, opting out of the default ride-along for this turn -- once it's moved on its own, it's no longer carried along automatically. There's no equivalent preemption for a combat move -- an air unit either flies its own explicit attack (a normal combat move) or, if it does nothing, may ride along with its carrier's move instead.
carrier_ride_along.chaining: an air unit that uses its own non-combat move to fly ONTO a carrier can still ride along for free when that carrier makes its own (separate) non-combat move later in the same phase -- the plane's own move gets it aboard, then the carrier's move carries it further, without that second leg counting as a second move for the plane.
carrier_ride_along.status: implemented for both move types. Non-Combat Move -- see engine.engine.GameEngine._execute_noncombat_moves: moving an Aircraft Carrier there sweeps along every one of the mover's air units CURRENTLY co-located in the carrier's origin, determined purely by physical presence at the moment the carrier's own order is processed (not a based_on_carrier lookup, and not gated on has_moved_noncombat) -- this single rule naturally covers the default ride-along (nothing there to exclude it), pre-emption (an earlier order already moved the plane AWAY, so it's simply not co-located anymore), and chaining (an earlier order flew the plane ONTO the carrier's zone, so it IS still co-located when the carrier's own later order runs, even though its own move already set has_moved_noncombat) all from one mechanism, since order-of-submission is what actually distinguishes the three cases, not any extra flag. Combat Move -- see _execute_combat_moves: uses a DIFFERENT model, since combat move has no valid 'chaining' reading (a plane can't meaningfully attack on its own and then also ride into a second attack the same phase) -- every air unit with its OWN explicit order anywhere in the submitted list is precomputed and excluded from ANY carrier's ride-along sweep in that same submission, regardless of whether its own order comes before or after the carrier's. A swept rider is simply relocated to the carrier's destination and marked has_moved_combat, and also picks up the same combat_move_origin/based_on_carrier bookkeeping an air unit's own combat move gets, making it eligible for return_to_base_after_combat too -- nothing else was needed to make it an actual combatant, since Combat Resolution's gather_battle_units already includes anyone physically present at a contested territory, however they got there.

open_water_anticipation.rule: an aircraft can never non-combat-move to a sea zone hoping SOME OTHER unit's own move order will bring a carrier there later the same phase -- not even the mover's own carrier's own move. It CAN move to a sea zone where its own Aircraft Carrier is already queued in this turn's pending_deployment (a fresh purchase arriving at the Deploy phase) -- that's a known, already-decided GameState fact, not a hope. An ally's carrier, present or pending, is never sufficient either way -- landing on water specifically requires the mover's own carrier (see air_landing_rule).
open_water_anticipation.status: implemented -- see engine/movement.py's legal_air_move_destinations, which checks TerritoryState.pending_deployment for the mover's own Aircraft Carrier

phase_confirmation.rollback_rule: During the Purchase, Combat Move, and Non-Combat Move phases, every order the active player submits is tentative and fully reversible -- any individual choice can be undone, or the whole phase rolled all the way back to how it stood when the phase began, right up until the player explicitly confirms that phase is complete. Nothing is committed to the persistent GameState until that confirmation.
phase_confirmation.scope: Applies only to these three phases. Combat Resolution is never reversible once it starts -- dice have been rolled and there is no mid-battle retreat (see combat.no_mid_battle_retreat); a battle's outcome, once resolved, stands. Capture Territory and Deploy + Income are automatic, derived consequences of the already-confirmed Combat Move / Non-Combat Move phases, not phases with their own player choices to roll back.
phase_confirmation.engine_note: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.submit_purchases/confirm_purchases, submit_combat_moves/confirm_combat_moves, submit_noncombat_moves/confirm_noncombat_moves. Each submit_* call validates and stages the CALLER'S COMPLETE desired order list for that phase (against a throwaway deep copy, so legal-destination queries see the buffer's current contents), replacing whatever was staged before -- resubmitting a shorter/corrected list IS how a caller undoes a prior choice; there's no separate undo_last()/reset_phase() call, since re-submission already covers it. Nothing lands in the real GameState until the matching confirm_* call, which is irreversible.

production.per_turn_deploy_cap_formula: value + (2 if strategic_center else 0) -- the SC bonus applies to both a territory's effective value for income (income_formula) AND its unit production/deploy limit here; the same +2, not two different numbers.
production.cap_scope: a pure unit-COUNT limit on newly-deployed units per LAND territory per turn -- not MPC-weighted, and distinct from setup.territory_stacking_cap_formula (which only applies at initial setup). There is no cap at all on total units already present in a territory -- only on how many new ones can land there in a single turn. A sea space draws its cap from an adjacent owned land territory instead of having one of its own -- see purchase.sea_deploy_cost_and_cap_source.
production.income_formula: sum of (value + 2 if strategic_center) over every territory the faction currently controls that ISN'T contested, collected at Deploy + Income -- territories.json carries a value and strategic_center field on every land space (confirmed present on all 87). A contested territory contributes to neither side's income, per combat.contested_territory_rule. Sea zones have no value field and generate no income.
production.income_formula_status: confirmed and implemented -- see engine/economy.py's compute_income(); every faction's real territories.json data sums to exactly the expected 31 MPC starting treasury (25 base value + 3 Strategic Centers x 2), verified by engine/tests/test_setup.py and test_economy.py.

purchase.location_rule: a purchase targets either a land territory the faction owns, or a sea zone adjacent to one it owns -- see multi_adjacent_allocation_order for a sea zone touching more than one owned territory. Ownership is checked against the START of the faction's own turn (see ownership_snapshot_rule) -- Purchase is the first phase, before that turn's own Combat Move/Resolution/Capture Territory can change anything, so a purchase can never target a territory the faction doesn't already control, even one its own combat this same turn might go on to capture.
purchase.ownership_snapshot_rule: a faction may only purchase at territories it controls at the beginning of its turn. This falls out naturally from the phase order (Purchase runs before any of this turn's own combat), but is called out explicitly to foreclose 'buy now, capture later this same turn' as a strategy.
purchase.unit_type_by_location: land and air units may be deployed to a land location. ANY unit type -- including land units, not just naval/air -- may instead be deployed directly to a sea space: a land unit deployed this way starts the game as Transport cargo, exactly as if it had entered water mid-move (see movement.water_movement_bonus_rule) -- there's still no such thing as an independently-purchased Transport.
purchase.sea_deploy_cost_and_cap_source: a sea space has no value or deploy cap of its own -- when units deploy there, the applicable per-unit cost (including any Strategic Center discount, see sc_discount_rule) and the per-turn deploy cap (production.per_turn_deploy_cap_formula) are both drawn from whichever adjacent OWNED land territory is being charged for that purchase.
purchase.sc_discount_rule: units.json's cheaper sc_cost applies whenever a purchase is charged against a Strategic Center -- whether the units deploy directly on that SC's own land territory, or to an adjacent sea space being charged against it (see sea_deploy_cost_and_cap_source). Not setup-specific -- applies on every ongoing turn's purchases too.
purchase.multi_adjacent_allocation_order: when a sea space touches more than one territory the purchasing faction owns, its deploy capacity is drawn from those adjacent territories in a fixed order: the Strategic Center first (if any of them is one), then whichever remaining territory has the most CAPACITY STILL UNUSED this turn -- not its raw/total value; if other purchases already this turn have eaten into a territory's cap, that lowers its priority here. A single purchase order SPILLS OVER automatically across this ordered list -- if the quantity purchased exceeds what the first source territory can still support, the remainder is drawn from the next territory in line, and so on, until the full quantity is placed or every eligible adjacent territory's capacity is exhausted (in which case the order is invalid). Cost (sc_cost vs cost) follows whichever territory the capacity is actually being drawn from at each point in that spillover -- a single order can mix sc_cost and cost units if it spills from an SC into a regular territory.
purchase.contested_land_deploy_restriction: only Infantry may be deployed into a contested LAND territory (combat.contested_territory_rule), and specifically onto the land itself -- being adjacent water doesn't create a loophole around this; the restriction is about the land territory's contested status, not about location type.
purchase.carrierless_air_deploy_fallback: if air units are purchased for deployment to a sea space and, once Deploy + Income actually runs, no Aircraft Carrier is present there or arriving there that same turn (neither pre-existing nor a fresh purchase), the air units deploy instead to the LAND territory they were purchased at, rather than being lost or left stranded.
purchase.contested_purchase_lost_during_turn_fall: if Infantry are purchased into a contested territory and that territory is then lost (captured by the enemy) before Deploy + Income runs, the units fall back in order: (1) an adjacent territory the faction still controls; (2) if none, an adjacent sea zone, deployed as Transport cargo (see unit_type_by_location); (3) if neither exists, the units are lost outright -- purchased but never placed, the MPC already spent.
purchase.hostile_sea_deploy_creates_contested: deploying units into a sea zone currently occupied by a non-ally makes that zone CONTESTED immediately, as a direct result of the deployment -- not silent co-occupation. The faction already there gets combat.first_round_bonuses' 'sea deploy into enemy-occupied zone' bonus in the first round of whatever battle eventually resolves the contest.
purchase.status: fully implemented, including the Deploy + Income consequences. GameEngine.submit_purchases/confirm_purchases (Purchase) cover location targeting, the start-of-turn ownership snapshot, SC-discounted cost, the SC-first-then-most-remaining-capacity multi-territory allocation with automatic spillover within a single order (UnitInstance.purchased_at records exactly which land territory funded each individual unit, since spillover can split one order across several), land/sea unit-category restrictions, and the contested-land Infantry-only restriction. GameEngine.deploy_and_collect_income (Deploy + Income) then covers carrierless_air_deploy_fallback, contested_purchase_lost_during_turn_fallback, and hostile_sea_deploy_creates_contested, using purchased_at to know where a redirected unit's land fallback is. Rollback matches phase_confirmation: submit_purchases takes the complete desired list each call (resubmitting is how a caller undoes a prior choice) and nothing touches treasury_mpc/pending_deployment until confirm_purchases, which is then irreversible for that faction's turn; Deploy + Income has no staging of its own since it's automatic by nature.

promotion.effect: permanent combat bonus: attack die steps up one size (max D12), +1 defense (max 10), +1 HP
promotion.demotion: not specified in the current design doc revision
promotion.service_record_note: every unit is tracked as an individual, persistent record (stable unit_id), not an anonymous stack count -- its XP, promotion status, and current damage/HP all persist on that specific unit across turns and battles.

faction_modes.human_bot: functionally identical to the engine -- both get full turns through the same order-submission API, full budget/production; differ only in who/what submits orders
faction_modes.defensive: seeded via the 100-IPC/no-SC scenario ruleset (see data/scenarios/starting_setup_100ipc.json). Never receives a turn: no purchases, no movement, no reinforcement, can't join alliances. Its territory IS capturable and its starting units DO fight back normally as an ordinary defender when attacked.
faction_modes.neutral: zero units, zero turns. Its territory is a hard exclusion from every other faction's legal move/attack targets -- not a combatant, an impassable region.

alliances.membership: FactionState.alliance is a plain membership tag (two factions are allied if it's set and equal) -- MOVEMENT and CAPTURE rules already consult it: own-or-allied territory/units count as friendly throughout movement, and combat.multi_party_battles pools allied defenders together. A faction can only be in one alliance at a time (rule 5) -- invite_to_alliance refuses to invite a target that's already in an alliance; it must withdraw first.
alliances.alliances_phase_action: During the Alliances phase (the 7th and last turn_order phase), a faction may optionally do ONE of two things this turn: invite_to_alliance (propose to a specific target faction) or withdraw_from_alliance (leave its current alliance). GameEngine._alliance_action_taken enforces the one-action-per-turn limit, reset each turn in advance_turn(). Doing neither is always legal (a no-op turn).

invite_to_alliance.flow: faction invites target; target_accepts is decided immediately by the caller (rule 6 -- 'when invited to join an alliance, a faction immediately decides to join or not'; the engine has no separate pending-invite state -- a driver/bot/human resolves the accept/reject decision itself and passes the result straight into invite_to_alliance's target_accepts argument).
invite_to_alliance.on_accept: joining an alliance means becoming aligned with ALL of its current members (rule 3), not just the inviter -- if faction is already in an alliance, target joins that same tag (everyone faction was already allied with); if neither is yet allied, a brand-new alliance tag is generated (GameState._next_alliance_id, e.g. 'ALLIANCE_1').
validation: faction and target must both be active (HUMAN/BOT) factions -- NEUTRAL/DEFENSIVE can't be invited (DEFENSIVE is explicitly documented elsewhere as unable to join alliances; NEUTRAL never takes any turn action at all).
target must not already be in an alliance (must withdraw first).

the PROSPECTIVE alliance (faction's current members, plus target) must not exceed _effective_max_alliance_size() -- see alliances.effective_max_alliance_size, not simply the raw game_start_settings.max_alliance_size value.
if can_rejoin_alliances is False (the default), target must not share a former_allies ban with anyone in the prospective alliance -- see rejoin_ban below.
must be faction's turn, Alliances phase, and faction's one alliance action for the turn not yet spent.

withdraw_from_alliance.effect: faction leaves its CURRENT alliance entirely -- no longer allied with any of its former members (rule 4), not just the one it might name.
withdraw_from_alliance.sc_lock: refuses (ValueError) if faction currently has any unit sitting on an allied Strategic Center it doesn't own -- the design doc's 'can't withdraw while you have units in an allied Strategic Center.' A unit on faction's OWN Strategic Center never blocks this.
withdraw_from_alliance.former_allies_tracking: for each former co-member, records the pair symmetrically in both factions' former_allies sets (used by the rejoin ban below).
withdraw_from_alliance.reclaim_setup: for every LAND territory owned by a former ally that faction is still physically occupying (units present) at the moment of withdrawal, marks it contested (t.contested_by |= {faction, owner}) and sets t.reclaim_bonus_for = owner -- see combat.first_round_bonuses' 'former-ally territory reclaim' case and combat.true_territory_loss's betrayal_exception for how that bonus (recurring, not one-shot) and the territory's protection from an instant loss both work while it stays set.
withdraw_from_alliance.no_special_end_of_game_window: there is NO separate 'last chance' withdrawal at game end -- victory.game_end_rule's check (GameEngine.process_game_end_check) is a pure query, run AFTER the Alliances phase's regular action has already happened. A faction wanting to withdraw to avoid the game ending from would_game_end()'s all-remaining-factions-allied condition must call withdraw_from_alliance itself, as its one regular Alliances-phase choice, same as any other turn -- confirmed this session after an earlier draft mistakenly built a bypass-the-guard special case into process_game_end_check; that was removed.

alliances.rejoin_ban: Default (can_rejoin_alliances=False): a faction that withdrew can never again share an alliance with anyone who was a co-member of that alliance AT THE MOMENT it withdrew -- a PAIRWISE ban recorded in former_allies, not a blanket 'never ally with anyone again' rule and not scoped to only the exact former alliance tag (a later alliance under a different tag containing any banned pair is still refused). invite_to_alliance checks the ban against the WHOLE prospective alliance (every current member plus the invitee), not just the two factions directly involved in the invite -- so a 3-faction alliance can't be reassembled piecemeal by inviting the banned faction back into an alliance with a different member it never personally withdrew from. When can_rejoin_alliances is True, former_allies is still recorded but never checked.
alliances.reclaim_bonus: See combat.first_round_bonuses' 'former-ally territory reclaim' case and combat.true_territory_loss's betrayal_exception -- both fully implemented. TerritoryState.reclaim_bonus_for names the one faction (the betrayed former owner) who gets the round-1 bonus every qualifying battle here, as attacker on its own turn or as defender if the betrayer attacks it instead, for as long as the flag stays set (confirmed this session: RECURRING, not consumed by a single attempt -- a failed counter-attack must not hand the territory to the betrayer). resolve_combat reads it before each battle; only process_capture_territory (or _apply_battle_outcome, if the betrayer's own attack fails outright) ever clears it, once the contest is genuinely resolved one way or the other.
alliances.design_doc_reference: 2 or 3 factions can join in alliances depending on game settings. Can withdraw from an alliance OR invite 1 faction to join at turn end; invited faction immediately accepts or rejects. Can't withdraw while you have units in an allied Strategic Center. Occupied former-ally territories become contested; the former ally gets a combat bonus in the first round of combat to reclaim them. Allies can move through each other's territories without claiming them; their units don't fight each other. Allies defend together. NOTE: the design doc's 'the attacker chooses which non-aligned faction they're attacking' is SUPERSEDED for this engine -- see combat.multi_party_battles, decided earlier this session: there's no picking a single target among several non-allied factions present, all of them defend together as one pooled side.
alliances.not_yet_built: Bot decision-making for WHEN to invite/accept/withdraw is now implemented too -- see bots.alliance_policy (a later session's follow-up to 'the engine, first'). Still not built: any HUMAN-facing UI for alliance actions.
alliances.effective_max_alliance_size: game_start_settings.max_alliance_size is a ceiling only -- see that entry and GameEngine._effective_max_alliance_size(): min(max_alliance_size, len(active_factions()) - 1), recomputed fresh every time invite_to_alliance is called.
