Confirmed this session: as players are eliminated, this reduces the cap; it does NOT force any existing alliance to dissolve, it only restricts what NEW alliances can be formed or grown into from that point on.

victory.elimination_rule: a faction is eliminated when it controls <=1 Strategic Center (original or captured); contested SCs still count as controlled (ownership only ever changes via Capture Territory, so a still-contested SC's registered owner hasn't lost it yet). Remove all remaining units from the board on elimination. Implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.process_elimination_check, meant to run right after Capture Territory each turn (automatic, no player choice, nothing to roll back). It's GameState.active_factions() excluding eliminated factions -- which every phase method already gates on, and which combat.recovery_rule's num_factions is derived from -- that actually enforces 'gets no more turns,' not anything phase-specific. NEUTRAL and DEFENSIVE are both exempt: neither ever has turns to lose, and a Defensive power has no Strategic Centers -- its units stay in play until they are individually killed (it is never eliminated).

game_end_rule.rule: the game ends when there are no unallied factions remaining -- every remaining active faction (GameState.active_factions(), i.e. HUMAN/BOT and not yet eliminated) must be mutually allied with every other. Since FactionState.alliance is a single tag per faction, that's exactly equivalent to all of them sharing the same one non-None alliance value (or trivially true with 1 or 0 active factions left).
game_end_rule.timing: checked once, at the very end of the ACTIVE faction's full turn -- after the Alliances phase (the last of the 7 turn_order phases) has run its regular invite/withdraw action, if any.
game_end_rule.status: implemented -- see engine.engine.GameEngine.would_game_end (pure query) and process_game_end_check, which is ALSO a pure query+set now (no longer applies any withdrawal itself): it just sets GameState.game_over to would_game_end()'s result. There is no special end-of-game withdrawal window -- a faction wanting to avoid the game ending must call withdraw_from_alliance itself, as its one regular Alliances-phase choice, before process_game_end_check runs -- see alliances.withdraw_from_alliance.no_special_end_of_game_window.

bots.status: implemented -- see engine.bots.random_bot.RandomBot and engine.bots.driver.play_to_completion. Not part of the rules themselves (a bot is just one possible caller of GameEngine's public phase API, same as a human UI would be) -- documented here only so the deliberately-unsophisticated policy behind a bot-driven test game is traceable back to an explicit decision, not mistaken for a rule.
bots.purpose: exercise the full turn loop end-to-end across many turns as an integration/stress test (docs/GAME_ARCHITECTURE.md build plan, Step 5) -- not to be a good opponent. No learning, no lookahead.
bots.purchase_policy: spend a random amount up to 55% of the treasury at Strategic-Center-associated targets -- a land SC itself, or a sea zone whose purchase would draw cost/capacity from an adjacent owned SC (GameEngine._purchase_sources is the source of truth for which sea zones qualify) -- then spend whatever's left randomly at every other legal target. Both passes repeatedly pick a random TARGET first, then a random unit type valid for that target -- a sea target's candidate pool never includes a Land-category unit type at all ('SCs should never produce land units in sea areas,' a bot defense policy, this session, applied to every sea target not just an SC-funded one -- GameEngine itself still allows a land unit purchased at sea, confirmed deliberate: it just starts out already mid-transit, no different from one that walked into hostile water and got swept up as cargo; this is a bot-policy choice, not an engine-level restriction) -- keeping the pick only if the growing order list stays legal and, for the SC pass, within its sub-budget. setup.excluded_naval_zones (the landlocked Caspian Sea, id 43) is never a candidate target at all, for any bot -- see engine.bots.policy.excluded_naval_purchase_zones, a shared rule this bot and every future bot in the package must apply, not something specific to RandomBot.
bots.combat_move_policy: for each of the bot's own units that hasn't combat-moved yet, make the first legal combat move found -- closest (fewest hops) legal destination, ties broken by lowest territory_id. The bot never retreats from a contested area via combat move -- in this engine that's only ever possible for a land unit mid-transit through hostile/contested water (movement.combat_move_destination's amphibious STOP_AND_PASS_LAND_ONLY exception is the sole way a combat move can legally end on safe, friendly territory; every other legal stop is already an attack, a capture, or joining a fight). For such a unit, the preference order is: an amphibious ATTACK (a land destination that's actually an attack/capture/join, not merely a safe landing) first, falling back to getting onto allied land only if no attack option exists this turn, falling back further to joining the naval battle in the sea zone itself only if no land option exists at all -- always trying to combat-move OUT of a sea battle rather than settling for it ('transported land units should seek land conflicts'). Sea units have no retreat option to begin with (open, uncontested water is never itself a legal combat-move stop), so any legal destination for one already fights to the end by construction.
bots.noncombat_move_policy: for each of the bot's own units that hasn't moved this turn, move toward the nearest enemy-OWNED land territory (read as ownership, matching how the rest of this ruleset uses the phrase) -- among the unit's own legal non-combat destinations, pick whichever minimizes remaining plain-adjacency graph distance to that target. A unit with no legal moves, or no enemy territory anywhere on the reachable graph, stays put.
bots.randomness_scope: Purchase, and target/withdrawal SELECTION among equally-valid alliance options, are randomized (this bot's own rng) -- Combat Move and Non-Combat Move are both deterministic given the board state, and WHETHER an alliance action happens at all follows each bot's fixed alliance_strategy/alliance_behavior rule, not randomness -- so a driven game is reproducible for a given RNG seed.
bots.defense_policy: an Infantry unit currently sitting on a Strategic Center the bot owns never moves at all, via combat move OR non-combat move, for the rest of the game -- it garrisons there permanently once it arrives, however it got there ('Infantry should never leave an SC... once they reach an SC, they just stay there,' this session). Checked fresh from the unit's current position every phase (RandomBot._garrisons_an_sc), so a later arrival is covered automatically with no separate tracked state. Scoped to Infantry specifically -- the ruleset's designated defensive garrison unit type (see purchase.contested_land_deploy_restriction) -- other land units on the same SC are unaffected.

alliance_policy.status: implemented -- see engine.bots.alliance_policy (the decision logic) and RandomBot.take_alliance_phase/_maybe_roll_treacherous_intent (the per-turn hook, called from engine.bots.driver.play_to_completion). Layered on top of alliances' engine mechanics, which only enforce validity, not strategy -- this module decides WHEN a bot invites/accepts/withdraws.
alliance_policy.game_start_settings: each BOT faction (never HUMAN/DEFENSIVE/NEUTRAL) gets two settings, resolved ONCE at setup.build_game_state time and stored on FactionState.alliance_strategy/alliance_behavior -- see that function's alliance_strategies/alliance_behaviors params. A 'random' input (or omitting a faction entirely) is rolled to one concrete value there and stays fixed for the rest of the game, even though bot decision logic itself may get more sophisticated later -- landing on 'variable' (see below) is exactly as permanent a result as landing on any other single value would have been; it's only the CONCRETE strategy/behavior actually driving decisions that keeps changing after that.

alliance_strategy.aggressive: always invites a random eligible faction (capped by max_alliance_size) if not yet at max size, wanting the largest possible alliance; also always accepts any invitation it receives -- grows via either path (confirmed this session).
alliance_strategy.passive: never invites; always accepts any invitation it receives.
alliance_strategy.counterweight: invites (randomly, among eligible factions) only to match the size of the CURRENT LARGEST other alliance on the board, never inviting past that size, and stops once matched -- recomputed fresh every turn, so it resumes inviting if a rival alliance later grows past it again. Does nothing at all while no other alliance yet exists anywhere on the board (confirmed this session: it does not found the first alliance itself). Applies that same 'never end up bigger than the largest other alliance' cap to ACCEPTING an invitation too (confirmed this session, not just to its own inviting) -- comparing the prospective merged alliance's size against the largest alliance other than the one it would be joining.
alliance_strategy.variable: added a later session: re-rolls to one of the four CONCRETE strategies above -- never variable or random themselves -- once at game start (so there's a real decision from turn 1, not None) and again at the start of every one of this bot's own turns, via engine.bots.alliance_policy.reroll_alliance_strategy, stored on FactionState.current_alliance_strategy (never overwriting alliance_strategy itself, which stays literally 'variable' all game). Every decision function reads the EFFECTIVE strategy via effective_alliance_strategy, which resolves 'variable' to whatever the latest re-roll landed on -- so a variable bot behaves exactly like a bot whose fixed strategy happened to be that turn's pick, no different logic needed anywhere else.

alliance_behavior.applicability: irrelevant whenever game_start_settings.can_withdraw_from_alliances is False -- withdrawing is simply never possible then, so no behavior's rule can ever fire (confirmed this session).
alliance_behavior.loyal: never withdraws, no exceptions -- ignores both the strength-mismatch rule below and the game-end override.
alliance_behavior.opportunistic: withdraws if it's now much stronger than its weakest CURRENT ally (current FactionState.treasury_mpc, or total deployed-unit cost, > 150% of that ally's) or much weaker than its strongest ally (< 50% of either metric) -- confirmed this session: 'MPC' means current treasury, not cumulative, and only deployed units need counting since the Alliances phase runs after Deploy + Income (purchase.pending_deployment is always empty by then). Compared independently per metric (OR'd, not AND'd) against every other current ally, not just one. ALSO always withdraws if the game would otherwise end on this faction's own turn (victory.game_end_rule via GameEngine.would_game_end()), overriding the strength check entirely -- confirmed this session.
alliance_behavior.treacherous: a 15% chance, rolled once at the very start of each of its own turns (RandomBot._maybe_roll_treacherous_intent, called from take_purchase_phase -- Purchase always being turn_order's first phase -- and only while actually in an alliance at that moment) to withdraw later that same turn's Alliances phase, regardless of any other factor; stored on FactionState.pending_treacherous_withdrawal until consumed there. Documented in the design conversation as deliberately simple for now ('this will get more sophisticated as bots evolve'). ALSO always withdraws if the game would otherwise end on this faction's own turn -- the same override opportunistic gets, confirmed this session to apply to treacherous too. Reads the EFFECTIVE behavior (effective_alliance_behavior), so a 'variable' bot whose re-roll landed on 'treacherous' this same turn rolls this 15% chance too.
alliance_behavior.variable: added a later session: same re-roll-every-turn idea as alliance_strategy's variable, over the three CONCRETE behaviors above -- FactionState.current_alliance_behavior, via reroll_alliance_behavior, re-rolled at game start and at the start of every one of this bot's own turns (RandomBot._maybe_reroll_variable_alliance_settings, called BEFORE _maybe_roll_treacherous_intent in take_purchase_phase, so a fresh 'treacherous' pick this same turn still gets its own 15% roll in time).

alliance_policy.action_priority: at most one alliance action per turn (engine.engine.GameEngine._alliance_action_taken enforces this authoritatively) -- RandomBot.take_alliance_phase checks alliance_behavior's withdrawal decision FIRST when currently allied, and only falls through to alliance_strategy's invite decision if it isn't withdrawing this turn; a bot that wants out has no reason to also try growing the alliance it's about to leave.

map.adjacency_source: Delaunay triangulation over territory center points (computed on a cylinder: the map wraps east-west, x=3500 is the same seam as x=0, so triangulation uses ghost copies of every point shifted by the map width; north-south does not wrap), edges kept under a 420px length threshold, plus a small hand-confirmed FORCED_EDGES list in tools/compute_adjacency.py for real adjacencies that threshold would otherwise wrongly exclude. Fully regenerable -- see tools/compute_adjacency.py. Every space in territories.json is a real graph node; there is no fallback category for territories added later.
map.foreign_neighbor_flag_definition: a land territory has at least one land neighbor belonging to a different faction
